title: Grain Accounting Manual: The Delayed Price Service Charge on Grain Marketing Contracts
content:
Bushels standing unpriced under Grain Marketing Contracts are carried at the member's cost once the free period is used up.

**Clause 1 — when the charge accrues.** The delayed price service charge accrues only while the contract stands in active, delivering or fully delivered, and stops accruing on a parcel the day that parcel is priced. The standing is read off the contract record against the contract number, and the parcel is correlated to it by the date it took its place in the unpriced position.

**Clause 2 — how far the count runs on a parcel still open.** The days a parcel has carried run through the day it is priced, or through the handling date where the parcel is still open.

**Clause 3 — the month.** A chargeable month is a month of 30 calendar days, and a part of a month counts as a whole one.

**Clause 4 — when the charge is taken.** The charge is never taken in advance: it is drawn onto the settlement statement the parcel is finally priced and settled on.

**Clause 5 — programmes with no free days and programmes with no delayed pricing.** Where a programme carries no free days at all the charge runs from the day of delivery, and where a programme does not allow price later at all no parcel can enter the unpriced position and this rule never engages.

## Clauses no longer in force

Three clauses of this rule are **no longer in force** and are carried here only so that no reader applies them:

> "Each parcel carries its own clock, so a member who delivered on three separate days carries three clocks and three minimums, and the elevator does not net them into one position."

> "Carry is counted in calendar days from the position date, the position date itself counting as day zero; the free days are taken off first, and what remains is grouped into thirty-day months with any part of a month counting as a whole one."

> "The charge is the monthly rate times the net bushels in the parcel times those chargeable months, and where that comes to less than the parcel minimum the minimum is taken instead."

## Points of judgement

A contract standing in settled carries no accrual, because settled is not one of the three standings named in clause 1. A parcel priced today stops accruing today. On a programme whose catalogue shows no free days, nothing is free and the carry runs from delivery. On a programme that does not open the unpriced position at all, the question does not arise.
